t: partition(): one function for any file
title: partition(): one function for any file
description: unstructured.partition.auto.partition() detects the file type and picks the right parser, so one call handles PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, emails, and images. Auto-partitioning removes the file-type switchboard from ETL code. It is the front door of the whole library.

demo.program:
print('from unstructured.partition.auto import partition')
print('elements = partition(filename="doc.pdf")')
demo.expected_output:
from unstructured.partition.auto import partition
elements = partition(filename="doc.pdf")

title: Elements: the typed building blocks
description: Partitioning returns typed Elements: Title, NarrativeText, ListItem, Table, Image, Header, Footer, and more, each with text and metadata (page number, coordinates, filename). Typed elements let downstream code treat a document as structure, not a blob. Tables stay tables instead of melting into paragraphs.

title: Partition strategies: fast vs hi_res
description: strategy='fast' extracts embedded text quickly; strategy='hi_res' runs layout detection and OCR for scanned PDFs and complex layouts. Fast is right for born-digital PDFs; hi_res is right for scans. Choosing per document class is the main performance lever.

demo.program:
print("partition(..., strategy='fast')    # born-digital")
print("partition(..., strategy='hi_res')  # scans, OCR")
demo.expected_output:
partition(..., strategy='fast')    # born-digital
partition(..., strategy='hi_res')  # scans, OCR

title: Chunking: chunk_by_title and basic
description: chunk_by_title() groups elements under their headings into coherent chunks; chunk_elements() packs elements to a max character count with overlap. Good chunks are what make RAG answers cite the right passage. Chunking strategy matters more than embedding model for retrieval quality.

title: Cleaning and staging functions
description: unstructured.cleaners strip bullets, extra whitespace, and ligatures; stagers serialize elements to JSON, CSV, or the format vector DBs expect. Cleaning normalizes the mess of real documents before embeddings see them. Staging is the handoff to the index.

title: Table extraction that survives
description: Tables partition into Table elements with text_as_html preserving structure, so downstream code can parse rows and columns instead of guessing from whitespace. For RAG, tables chunked with their captions answer 'what was Q3 revenue' correctly. Structure preservation is the point.

description: Every element carries metadata: filename, page_number, coordinates on the page, and detected languages. Page numbers power 'see page 12' citations in RAG answers; coordinates power highlight-the-source UIs. Metadata is what turns chunks into evidence.

title: OCR integration for scans
description: hi_res partitioning uses Tesseract or PaddleOCR under the hood for image-based PDFs, with language packs selectable per document. OCR quality settings trade speed for accuracy on bad scans. Scanned archives become searchable without separate OCR tooling.

title: Email and HTML handling
description: MSG/EML emails partition into subject, sender, and body elements; HTML partitions preserve heading structure for chunk_by_title. Real corpora are full of emails and web pages, so first-class support matters. Structure-aware parsing beats text-dumping every time.

title: Deduplication helpers
description: The library includes helpers to drop duplicate elements and near-duplicate chunks, which cleans the repeated headers/footers that pollute indexes. Dedupe before embedding saves index space and stops the same footer winning every retrieval. Small helper, big quality win.

title: Language detection per element
description: Elements carry detected languages, so multilingual corpora can route chunks to the right embedding model or filter by language at query time. Language-aware pipelines avoid the garbage of wrong-language embeddings. Metadata does the routing.

title: The hosted API option
description: Unstructured also offers a hosted API with the same partition/chunk semantics for teams that do not want to manage OCR and model dependencies. The open-source library and the API share element schemas, so migration is painless. Self-host or SaaS, same data model.

title: Pipeline pattern: partition-chunk-embed
description: The canonical pipeline is partition -> clean -> chunk -> stage -> embed -> upsert, each step a library call. This five-step shape fits every document ETL and is easy to schedule and monitor. Standard shape, standard tooling, fewer surprises.

title: When not to use it
description: For pure born-digital text extraction at massive scale, lighter tools (PyPDF, pdfplumber) are faster; Unstructured earns its keep on messy, mixed, scanned corpora where structure matters. Knowing when the heavy tool is overkill is part of using it well. Right tool, right corpus.
